ApiLanguage.description: The REST API server language. GO (the default) emits the chi server module, RUST the axum crate, TYPESCRIPT the Hono package built on the TypeScript HTTP runtime (`<out>/api/<service>`, `<scope>/<service>-api`).

ApiOutputConfig.description: The REST API server. The server imports the service's types in its language, so an enabled API needs that language enabled in types: go for GO (the default), rust for RUST, typescript for TYPESCRIPT.

mcp.description: Serve the operations the mcp decorator makes visible tools over MCP at POST /api/mcp (D81): the caller authenticates as on the API's other routes, and each tools/call runs through the route of its operation. A TypeScript API serves it; the build refuses it on a Go or Rust API, where support follows. Unset is off.

CiOutputConfig.description: The CI a Stack service's build writes, keyed by the renderer that writes it: github for GitHub Actions, or a renderer an extension registers. Only a Stack service sets it. The build writes each workflow under <out>/ci/<stack>/.

CiRendererConfig.description: One CI renderer's options for a Stack service's generated workflow.

branch.description: The branch pull requests target and a push deploys from: a branch name, not a pattern. Unset is "main".

install.description: The directory, relative to the repository root, the build installs the workflow into when it exists. Unset is the renderer's own, .github/workflows for github.

EngineAccessRule.description: One rule of an engine's access policy, as the engine reads it.

EngineOutputConfig.description: A DB service's engine document (D58), which the build writes when a type of the schema composes a behavior: an engine type, whose instances the engine keeps, which sql and orm leave out.

mount.description: The path a server of an API on this database mounts the engine's routes at, its event stream and its MCP endpoint under it: one or more segments, each of letters, digits and . _ ~ -. Unset is /engine/<service>.

namespace.description: The engine namespace the schema's engine types are defined, published and instantiated in: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters. Unset is the service's name.

policy.description: The access policy the servers open the engine with: "permission", which allows an action on a type to a caller holding <Type>.<action> (Ticket.read, Ticket.write, Ticket.define, Ticket.publish); "allowAll", for tests and local use; or ordered rules, the first that matches a question deciding it. Unset is "permission".

retention.description: How long the engine's event log keeps events: an age, a count or both, as the engine reads them. Every server, job, worker and runner on this database opens the engine with it, and the database's runner prunes the log, never past an event a reaction has yet to handle. Unset keeps every event.

tools.description: The engine's tool options the deployment sets beside the binary's invocation policy and vendor keys (D70).

EnginePolicy.description: An engine's access policy (D58): a shorthand, or ordered rules, each matching on the question's action, operation, schema and namespace and the caller's subject and service, and either naming a permission the principal must hold or allowing or refusing outright. The engine checks the rules when a server opens it.

batchSize.description: Events pruned in one transaction. Unset is 1000.

everyMs.description: How often the runner prunes, in milliseconds. Unset is 60000.

maxAgeMs.description: Events older than this many milliseconds, by when they were written, are pruned.

maxEvents.description: A namespace's events past its newest this many are pruned.

maxHoldMs.description: The longest a reaction that does not advance (halted, in an archived namespace, or whose behavior the engine does not run) holds events retention lets go, in milliseconds. Unset, one that has run holds them until it advances, and one that has not holds none.

batchSize.description: Events pruned in one transaction. Unset is 1000.

everyMs.description: How often the runner prunes, in milliseconds. Unset is 60000.

maxAgeMs.description: Events older than this many milliseconds, by when they were written, are pruned.

maxEvents.description: A namespace's events past its newest this many are pruned.

maxHoldMs.description: The longest a reaction that does not advance (halted, in an archived namespace, or whose behavior the engine does not run) holds events retention lets go, in milliseconds. Unset, one that has run holds them until it advances, and one that has not holds none.

EngineRetention.description: The event log's retention (D58): maxAgeMs, maxEvents or both; an event goes when either lets it go. A stream or read that resumes from a cursor retention has pruned past is 410 cursor_expired.

EngineToolsConfig.description: What a deployment sets of the engine's tool options (D11, D70).

hidden.description: Behavior operations, by <Behavior>.<operation>, that the engine's MCP tools leave out: a service calls them through the API or in-process, and no agent is offered them. The build refuses a name no engine type's behavior declares, and the engine document adds the service operations of the core's commerce behaviors (Payments' listPaymentActions, recordPaymentEvent and settleRefundFor) wherever they are composed.

invocation.description: The MCP invocation policy of an engine tool or operation, by the name the engine's tools.invocation takes: a built-in tool's (create, delete, defineSchema), or a behavior operation's, <Behavior>.<operation> (Payments.capturePayment), in place of its declaration's. Each value is one of the binary's invocation policy's values (auto or ask in the core). The build refuses a name no engine type's behavior declares, and where the engine types compose Payments or Stock it refuses a map that does not name each of their operations that move money or stock (Payments' openPayment, capturePayment, voidPayment, refundPayment and refundFor; Stock's receiveStock, adjustStock and countStock). Every server, job, worker and runner on this database opens the engine with it, so an agent's MCP client asks before it runs an operation marked ask.

ExtensionKind.description: The name of a kind an extension registers ("Catalog"). The authoring packages cannot see the registry, so the name is any string here; superschematic checks it against the registered kinds when it loads the config.

SchemaConfigDocument.description:
The schema.config.json / schema.config.yaml document shape.

This is the SchemaConfig contract projected onto plain data: authDb is the service name, and dependencies and calls are explicit arrays of name + kind pairs (there is no import system in the JSON/YAML forms to derive them from). superschematic validates the data forms against the JSON Schema generated from this type (see the gen-json-schema package script).

buckets.description: The Bucket services this API's implementation uses: each is a Bucket in its Deps, and a bucket edge from its server and jobs. Only an API service sets it, and each entry names a Bucket service.

calls.description: The API services this API's implementation calls, or this site's code calls from the browser. Only an API or a Site service sets it, and each entry names an API service. Each callee is built before its caller.

memoryStores.description: The MemoryStore services this API's implementation uses: each is a MemoryStore in its Deps, and a memoryStore edge from its server, jobs and workers. Only an API service sets it, and each entry names a MemoryStore service.

outputs.description: The generated outputs. A Site service has none, and may leave it out.

rateLimitStore.description: The MemoryStore service this API's rate-limited routes count in, so its replicas share one budget per client; while the store is unavailable each replica counts in process. It is listed in memoryStores whether or not that list names it. Only an API service sets it.

site.description: How a Site service builds and what it serves. Only a Site service sets it.

SchemaKind.description: The kinds the core compiler registers. Closed: an extension adds a kind by registering it with superschematic, not by extending this enum. A Stack service declares what runs where over the others (`@superschematic/stack`) and is named by none, so it has no sentinel. A Site service is a static site: its config names the APIs it calls and how it builds, and its code sits at its implementation path (D55). A Bucket service is private object storage that APIs list in their `buckets` (D54): its config is all it has, `{ name, kind: SchemaKind.Bucket, outputs: {} }`. A MemoryStore service is a Redis or Valkey server the replicas of a stack share, which holds no fact (D75): its schema declares each channel and key it carries (`@superschematic/memory-store`), and APIs list it in their `memoryStores`.

SchemaKindName.description: What a config's `kind` admits: a core SchemaKind member or an extension kind name.

SchemaOutputsDocument.description: The outputs block of the data forms: the core keys, plus the output key of any generator an extension registers. The authoring packages cannot see the registry, so an extension key is any name here; superschematic checks each key against the registered generators, and each section against its generator's OutputSchema, when it reads the config.

SdkOutputConfig.description: The client SDK in each language. An SDK imports the service's types in its language, so each enabled SDK language needs the same language enabled in types.

ServiceDependencyRef.description: A service reference in the JSON/YAML config forms, in dependencies, calls, buckets, memoryStores and rateLimitStore. The TypeScript form builds ServiceHandle sentinels with the service() helper; the data forms carry the same name + kind pair as a plain object.

SiteConfig.description: How a Site service builds and what it serves (D55). Its code is the package at the naming file's [implementation_paths] site template, web/{service} unless set, a member of the Bun workspace.

build.description: The script of the site's package.json that builds it, which a deploy runs with bun run after a frozen install of the workspace. Unset is "build".

fallback.description: The file, relative to output, served for a path that names no file: "index.html" for a single-page application, whose router reads the path. Unset answers such a path 404.

output.description: The directory the build writes, relative to the site's directory and inside it. Unset is "dist".

SqlDialect.description: A database the DB kind's sql output is built for.

SqlOutputConfig.description: The DB kind's sql output. The DDL and the ORM are implied by the kind; this block places and owns the generated projection view migrations and lists the dialects the DDL is written for.

dialects.description: The databases the service is built for. With sqlite listed, the build also writes sqlite/create.sql and refuses a schema that uses what SQLite does not support, and migrate plan --dialect sqlite plans for it. The list must hold postgres: the Go ORM the kind always generates runs on Postgres. Unset is ["postgres"].

migrationsDir.description: Where the projection view migrations are written, relative to the service directory. Unset keeps them under <out>/sql/<service>/projections/migrations.

sourceSchema.description: The Postgres schema that holds the tables the views read: each view selects <sourceSchema>.<table> for its source table and every joined table, so it does not depend on the migration runner's search_path. Unset leaves the tables unqualified.

viewOwner.description: The Postgres role the migrations create the views as: SET ROLE around the view DDL and RESET ROLE after it, so the schema's default privileges for that role apply. The migration runner must be a member of the role. Unset creates the views as the runner.

TypesOutputConfig.description: The type library in each language. A library imports the types of every dependency it takes types from, so each such dependency must enable the same languages; build-all and build --with-deps refuse a build where one does not. A DB schema needs go: the Go ORM the kind always generates imports the Go types.
